osps_ac_01_01_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide: GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation, covering repository write access and private vulnerability reports alike.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: Collaborator permissions are assigned explicitly, never inherited by default: the organisation baseline in settings-as-code sets the default repository permission to the lowest privilege, and the GitHub Actions token defaults to read-only here (default_workflow_permissions: read, read from the API on 2026-11-15). Write access comes only from membership of the owners team. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_03_01_justification: An organisation-level ruleset blocks direct pushes to main: every change must arrive as a pull request and pass required status checks. The rules and their rationale are recorded in docs/rulesets.md and the Monday audit re-checks them for drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The organisation ruleset restricts branch deletion on the primary branch, so deleting main is refused rather than confirmed away. Recorded in docs/rulesets.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Least privilege is the default and the explicit setting: the repository baseline sets the workflow token to read-only permissions, and every workflow declares its own minimal `permissions:` block on top of that. A job that specifies nothing therefore gets read, not write. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow declares an explicit `permissions:` block scoped to what that job actually needs, on top of a read-only default set by the repository baseline. The strongest case is enforced by a lint: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may hold `id-token: write`, and lint:capability-boundary fails the build if one ever does.
osps_br_01_01_justification: sign.yml never interpolates caller input into a shell: every input is routed through env as UNTRUSTED_*, the subject manifest is accepted only line by line as sha256sum records, an image digest only as sha256:<64 hex>, a predicate type only from an explicit allowlist and a predicate only as one JSON object, and anything else fails the job. zizmor checks for template injection in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: This is the project's central architectural rule, not an incidental setting: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may declare `id-token: write`. lint:capability-boundary enforces it in the gate and fails the build if a `workflow_call` workflow ever acquires the privileged identity, so a certificate bearing this repository's identity can never be minted by a job executing a caller's code.
osps_br_01_04_justification: Caller-supplied input is validated before use, never trusted: sign.yml's validation step accepts the subject manifest only as sha256sum records (at most 1024), an image only as a lowercase name plus sha256:<64 hex>, and a predicate type only from its allowlist. Offending values are not echoed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: This repository publishes no releases and no tags: it is one reusable workflow, and every consumer pins it by full 40-hex commit SHA (`uses: monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml@<sha>`) and verifies with --signer-digest against that commit. No official release is ever created, so there is none to assign a version identifier to; the commit SHA consumers pin is itself unique and immutable.
osps_br_02_02_justification: This repository publishes no releases and no tags: it is one reusable workflow, and every consumer pins it by full 40-hex commit SHA (`uses: monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml@<sha>`) and verifies with --signer-digest against that commit. With no release there are no release assets to associate with an identifier.
osps_br_03_01_justification: The only official channel is this GitHub repository, with its issue tracker, served over HTTPS; no plaintext http:// URI appears in any tracked file. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
osps_br_03_02_justification: The only distribution channel is this GitHub repository, served over HTTPS, and every consumer references it by full commit SHA, which authenticates the exact content fetched: git's content addressing makes a substituted workflow a different SHA. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
osps_br_04_01_justification: This repository publishes no releases and no tags: it is one reusable workflow, and every consumer pins it by full 40-hex commit SHA (`uses: monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml@<sha>`) and verifies with --signer-digest against that commit. No official release is created, so there is no release to carry a change log.
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependency ingestion is standardised: the only dependencies are GitHub actions and the organisation's shared workflows, each referenced by full commit SHA with its version in a comment (enforced by lint:action-pins) and updated by Renovate. mise.toml deliberately declares no language toolchain, so no package manager is used. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/renovate.json
osps_br_06_01_justification: This repository publishes no releases and no tags: it is one reusable workflow, and every consumer pins it by full 40-hex commit SHA (`uses: monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml@<sha>`) and verifies with --signer-digest against that commit. No official release is created, so there is no release to sign. Each push to main is instead given a signed source-provenance link by .github/workflows/source-attest.yml. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/source-attest.yml
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, so an unencrypted credential is blocked at push time; trivy's secret rules also run in the gate. The architecture removes most of the risk at source: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, so there are few long-lived secrets to leak.
osps_br_07_02_justification: docs/continuity.md is the secrets policy in operational form: an asset table naming every credential the project uses, where it is stored, who can reach it, and how it is rotated or recreated — including the one standing token, whose expiry is designed to fail loudly rather than silently under-claim. The policy is short because the architecture removes most secrets: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, and no signing key exists to store. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_do_01_01_justification: README.md documents basic use: what sign.yml does, the one subject shape per call, and the exact permissions a caller grants; each workflow_call input and output carries its own description in sign.yml. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the repository's issue forms document how to report a defect, and SECURITY.md documents the separate private path for vulnerabilities. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
osps_do_03_01_justification: This repository has made no release and has no tags: consumers pin sign.yml by full commit SHA. There are no release assets whose integrity needs verifying instructions. (The organisation's runbook documents verifying artifacts signed by this workflow, which is a different project's release.)
osps_do_03_02_justification: This repository has made no release and has no tags: consumers pin sign.yml by full commit SHA. There is no release whose author identity needs verifying.
osps_do_04_01_justification: This repository has made no release and has no tags: consumers pin sign.yml by full commit SHA. There is no release to state a support scope and duration for; SECURITY.md's roll-forward policy means only the tip of main is maintained. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: This repository has made no release and has no tags: consumers pin sign.yml by full commit SHA. There is no release to declare end of security updates for; SECURITY.md's roll-forward policy means only the tip of main is maintained. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: Documented in two places and deliberately so: docs/tooling-verdicts.md records how a dependency is selected — the priors a tool must meet to enter the belt, and the verdicts on tools considered and declined — and docs/dependency-track.md records how dependencies are obtained, pinned, monitored and triaged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/tooling-verdicts.md
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the whole sequence: `mise trust && mise install` brings the organisation's pinned toolchain, and `mise run ci` runs exactly what CI runs. This repository adds no tools of its own (mise.toml has an empty [tools] table). https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: docs/continuity.md carries an asset table naming who holds each sensitive resource — organisation ownership, the tag-mint App key, registry accounts, the one standing token — and what happens to each if that person is unavailable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and is served from the organisation's .github repository as the default community health file, which applies here because this repository has no GOVERNANCE.md of its own. The maintainer role is the @monumental-archive/owners team. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests on this repository are open for public discussion of changes and usage obstacles; both are searchable and addressable by URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: open an issue first for anything large, pull requests for small self-contained fixes, Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, a green `mise run ci`, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md includes a 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: pull request only, a green `mise run ci`, Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects under 72 columns, DCO sign-off, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Escalation and permissions' carries the policy: a collaborator is reviewed before being granted any escalated permission. Concretely, before an account joins @monumental-archive/owners or receives write access anywhere, the maintainer reviews who they are, why the access is needed and what the smallest sufficient grant is - and the grant is then recorded in the settings-as-code baseline so drift is auditable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#escalation-and-permissions
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 sign-off asserting legal authorisation. The commit-msg hook catches a missing trailer locally and lint:dco fails the gate, with no exemption list — automation signs off too.
osps_le_02_02_justification: This repository has made no release and has no tags: consumers pin sign.yml by full commit SHA. There are no released assets; the source itself is 0BSD. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt; api.reuse.software reports this repository compliant (checked 2026-11-15). https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: This repository has made no release and has no tags: consumers pin sign.yml by full commit SHA. There are no released assets to include a licence in.
osps_qa_01_01_justification: Publicly readable at a static URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, for every revision, and the history is public. Beyond that, each revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation, so the record is independently verifiable rather than merely readable.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: The direct dependencies are the actions and shared workflows named in .github/workflows/, each pinned to a full commit SHA with its version in a comment; Renovate reads them there. There is no language package manifest because there is no language toolchain. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: No compiled software is released: this repository publishes no releases, and its only product is sign.yml, a YAML workflow consumed by commit SHA. There is no released artifact for an SBOM to describe. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The gate is a required status check on main under an organisation ruleset: a pull request cannot merge red, and direct pushes are blocked entirely, so no commit reaches the primary branch without its checks passing. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project is this single repository with no subprojects; README.md states its contents are one signing workflow plus the organisation's stubs. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
osps_qa_04_02_justification: This repository has made no release and has no tags: consumers pin sign.yml by full commit SHA. There is no release, of one source repository or several.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable artifacts are committed: the tracked tree is workflow YAML, Markdown, TOML, JSON and licence text. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No unreviewable binary artifacts are committed — every tracked file is text and reviewable in a diff.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: gate.yml runs the organisation gate, `mise run ci` over every tracked file, on each pull request, and it is a required status check, so a change cannot be accepted before it passes. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states that `mise run ci` locally is exactly what CI runs and makes a green gate a requirement; gate.yml shows when it runs: every pull request, every push to main and the merge queue. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions', is the policy and it sits in the contributor-facing documentation: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, or a lint, audit task or workflow assertion where the product is configuration and policy - and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_07_01_justification: With a single maintainer there is no non-author human approval available, so this is not enforced. It is the headcount wall this project records rather than works around: the same boundary as Gold's two_person_review and SLSA Source L4, tracked as an open issue rather than quietly claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
osps_sa_01_01_justification: docs/release.md specifies the pipeline actor by actor and action by action — what each workflow does, which identity it runs as, what it is permitted to touch — and docs/build-track.md and docs/source-track.md carry the per-track designs. The capability boundary between caller code and the privileged identity is stated explicitly as a design rule. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/release.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The external interfaces are the reusable workflows and the task contract: docs/runbook.md documents each workflow's inputs and the artifact classes with their required parameters, and workflow-templates/ ships a caller stub per workflow. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
osps_sa_03_01_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are written security assessments of this system: they walk the controls, name the most likely and impactful failure modes (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, supply-chain substitution through unpinned dependencies, silent settings drift), and record which are mitigated and which are accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md carry the threat model and attack-surface analysis: the critical paths are named (caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, silent settings drift, forged signer identities in the transparency log), each with the control that protects it and the residual risk accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy and it states the timeframe: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, and what the reporter can expect afterwards. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the reporting channel: private vulnerability reporting through the repository's Security tab, with a 14-day acknowledgement commitment. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, delivering the report directly to the security contact without public exposure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerability data would be published as GitHub Security Advisories on this repository, the channel SECURITY.md names. No vulnerability in this repository's code has been reported to date. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_04_02_justification: No vulnerability has been reported in this repository's components: Dependabot reported 0 alerts on 2026-11-15, and the components are SHA-pinned GitHub actions. With no such vulnerability there is nothing to state non-exploitability for.
osps_vm_05_01_justification: dependency-review.yml runs on every pull request through the organisation's shared workflow, which fails on any newly introduced dependency with an advisory of high severity or above; the policy is written in the organisation's dependency-track.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_05_02_justification: This repository has made no release and has no tags: consumers pin sign.yml by full commit SHA. There is no release to hold back; on every pull request dependency-review blocks a newly introduced high-severity advisory. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Automatically, on every change: dependency-review runs on every pull request, the Monday audit runs the organisation's dependency advisory feed, and Renovate raises updates to the pinned actions. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md 'Static analysis policy' sets the remediation threshold at zero: any SAST finding fails the gate, and a red gate cannot merge. CodeQL has no open alert here; the four open code-scanning alerts are Scorecard posture checks (CodeReview, BranchProtection, Fuzzing, CII-Best-Practices), not code findings. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_06_02_justification: Every change is automatically evaluated and blocked on a finding: CodeQL default setup runs here, and actionlint, shellcheck, zizmor and trivy run in the gate, a required status check. The threshold is stated in SECURITY.md (see osps_vm_06_01). https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
access_continuity_justification: docs/continuity.md is exactly this document: assets and their recovery paths, a break-glass procedure for the tag-minting App, a succession plan, and an explicit list of deliberate single points of failure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project has no bespoke website: documentation is plain Markdown rendered by GitHub, which is keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly, and the content is text with descriptive link text rather than images carrying meaning.
assurance_case_justification: docs/release.md and docs/slsa-reference.md are the written assurance case, and docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md assess each claim against its evidence: the threat model (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, tampered artifacts), the countermeasures (the capability boundary, SHA pinning with checksums and attestations, keyless signing with transparency-log evidence), and an explicit record of what is NOT claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: gate.yml runs the organisation gate on every pull request (opened, synchronize, reopened, edited), on every push to main and in the merge queue, and it is a required check, so every change is integrated and checked before it lands. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
build_common_tools_justification: Nothing is built to use this software: sign.yml is a GitHub Actions reusable workflow, consumed by reference at a commit SHA, and mise.toml deliberately declares no language toolchain ('a signer with a compiler in it is a signer with a build in it').
build_floss_tools_justification: Nothing is built to use this software, so there are no build tools: sign.yml is consumed by reference at a commit SHA. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
build_non_recursive_justification: There is no build system to recurse: the repository holds workflows and documentation only and compiles nothing. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
build_preserve_debug_justification: Nothing is compiled or installed, so there is no debug information to strip or preserve. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
build_repeatable_justification: No building occurs in this repository at all: there is no release workflow, no publish stub and no artifact class, and level.yml declares `tracks: source` because the repository bears no build evidence. sign.yml signs digests other repositories' builds computed; it builds nothing itself. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/level.yml
build_reproducible_justification: No building occurs in this repository: there is no release workflow, no publish stub and no artifact class, and level.yml declares `tracks: source`. The sign.yml header records that reproducible builds in the calling repositories are what close the signer's residual, not anything built here. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries are generated: the repository is YAML and Markdown, with no compiler or linker invocation for CC, CFLAGS, CXX, CXXFLAGS or LDFLAGS to be passed to.
build_justification: The software requires no building for use: sign.yml is a reusable GitHub Actions workflow that callers reference by commit SHA, and nothing is compiled to run it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 — a single maintainer. Recorded plainly in docs/slsa-reference.md as headcount-blocked, with docs/continuity.md carrying the succession and break-glass paths that exist precisely because of it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the repository root, in the standard location, and served as the organisation default to every repository in the org. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Code review' documents how review is conducted and what must be checked: that the change does what it says, that the claim it makes is one its checks actually enforce, that it does not weaken a documented control, and that documentation changed alongside behaviour - with the mechanical floor (formatting, linting, licence headers, commit shape, tests) left to the CI gate rather than the reviewer. What is required to be acceptable is stated too: a green gate, resolved review threads enforced by ruleset, a DCO sign-off on every commit, and a PR title and body fit to become the permanent squash commit. It also records that with one maintainer there is no second human reviewer, and names the gate as the compensating control. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Automatically, in the gate: shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor, rumdl, typos and committed all run in `mise run ci` on every pull request, and `fix:*` siblings apply the machine-fixable subset. Style is never a review comment here.
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the gate as the coding standard in executable form, and the standards are specific per language: shellcheck for shell (with bash pinned by `[task_config] shell` because Ubuntu's sh is dash), actionlint and zizmor for workflow YAML, rumdl for Markdown, typos for spelling with the locale registers written down, and Conventional Commits with a 72-column subject ceiling. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the process explicitly: fork/branch, conventional imperative commit subjects under 72 columns enforced by committed, DCO sign-off, `mise run ci` green locally, pull request, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: every change arrives by pull request, must pass `mise run ci` (the coding standard in executable form), uses Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects, and is squash-merged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: There is one significant contributor, so there cannot be two unassociated ones. Headcount, not policy: contributions are welcomed under CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
copyright_per_file_justification: Every file carries a copyright statement through REUSE.toml, the REUSE specification's mechanism for files that cannot carry headers; `reuse lint` reports 17 of 17 files with copyright information and lint:reuse enforces it in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/REUSE.toml
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The project implements no cryptography and selects no algorithms; where cryptography is used it is Sigstore's and GitHub's, whose algorithm choices the project does not control.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic operations are delegated to software built for the purpose — Sigstore/cosign, GitHub's attestation tooling and git — never reimplemented here.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Nothing in the tree disables certificate verification: there is no `--insecure`, `curl -k`, `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` or plaintext http:// URL in any tracked file. sign.yml makes its only network calls through first-party SHA-pinned actions (actions/attest, actions/upload-artifact), which verify certificates by default. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software stores no authentication credentials or private keys at all. Secrets live in GitHub environment and organisation secrets, never in files in the repository, and release signing uses ephemeral keys.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography relied on is implementable with FLOSS: Sigstore, cosign and git are open source.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project selects no keylengths. Release signing uses ephemeral Sigstore keys with Fulcio-issued certificates, and transport keys belong to GitHub.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software stores no passwords and authenticates no external users.
crypto_pfs_justification: The software implements no key agreement protocol; it is configuration and workflows, not a network service.
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptography of its own. Where it relies on cryptography it uses published, expert-reviewed mechanisms: Sigstore (Fulcio certificates, Rekor transparency log), GitHub artifact attestations, SHA-256 checksums and OpenPGP-free keyless signing.
crypto_random_justification: The software generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; release signing keys are generated by Sigstore.
crypto_tls12_justification: The software implements and configures no TLS: its network traffic is made by GitHub-maintained actions and the runner, whose TLS versions are theirs.
crypto_used_network_justification: All network communication is HTTPS: sign.yml's attestation step talks to Sigstore (Fulcio, Rekor) and GitHub's attestation store through actions/attest, and no insecure protocol appears anywhere in the tree. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The software implements no HTTP client of its own and sends no headers itself; the OIDC token used for signing is requested and presented by the first-party actions/attest action, not by code in this repository.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The software's own mechanism uses SHA-256 only: sign.yml accepts subjects only as SHA-256 digests and signs with Sigstore's ECDSA P-256. Its action references are git commit IDs, the platform's only immutable pin form. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is depended on: subject integrity is SHA-256 (sign.yml accepts no other digest) and signing is Sigstore's ECDSA P-256. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1: every commit must carry Signed-off-by; the commit-msg hook catches it locally and lint:dco enforces it in this repository's gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
delivery_mitm_justification: Delivered over HTTPS by GitHub, and consumers reference sign.yml by full commit SHA, so the content they run is fixed by its hash, not by the transport alone. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is fetched over http: each consumer commits the full commit SHA it pins in its own `uses:` line, and verification derives --signer-digest from that pin. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
dependency_monitoring_justification: Renovate (renovate.json, extending the organisation preset) keeps every pinned action current and maintains the Dependency Dashboard issue; dependency-review.yml checks every pull request; audit.yml runs the organisation's dependency advisory feed every Monday. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/renovate.json
description_good_justification: The README's first lines say what it is: 'The org's signing identity, and nothing else' - one job that receives artifact digests from a caller and signs them, running no caller-supplied code. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests on this repository: searchable, addressable by URL, open to new participants and archived publicly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/issues
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page carries the badge block (gate, OpenSSF Scorecard, SLSA source level, REUSE, licence, fair-software), rendered by `mise run fix:badges` from .badge-states and checked by lint:badges in the gate so it cannot drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: README.md's 'Why it is separate' section explains the design (the signing workflow is the SLSA builder.id, so it must be unreachable from caller build steps) and the sign.yml header documents the capability boundary, the permission contract and the stated residuals. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
documentation_basics_justification: README.md documents what the workflow does, the subject shapes it accepts and the permissions it holds, and each sign.yml input and output carries its own description; the organisation's docs/release.md and docs/runbook.md give the surrounding orchestration. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is sign.yml's workflow_call contract: every input (subjects, image-name, image-digest, predicate-type, predicate, bundle-artifact) and output is documented in place, and README.md states the one-subject-shape rule and the exact permissions a caller must grant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/direction.md is the roadmap and it is unusually explicit about what the project will NOT do: a target table naming the level intended on each SLSA track, the claims policy, and the ceilings and why each sits where it does (BuildEnv is L0 by attribution, not by choice: its controls are built, but the signed build-image provenance that would make them a level belongs to producers who do not emit it; Gold-level criteria are not claimed while there is one maintainer). Open items are tracked as issues and the table is the first thing a closing issue updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/direction.md
documentation_security_justification: README.md states the security properties claimed (no caller-supplied code, no contents: write, an allowlisted predicate surface) and sign.yml's header states the residuals not closed - a compromised caller build can ask for any digest or allowlisted claim to be signed - and why. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis runs against this repository, so there is no build with assertions to enable. The nearest equivalent is always on: sign.yml's validation step runs under `set -euo pipefail` and fails the job on any input that is not whitelist-shaped.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is performed on this repository (see dynamic_analysis), so there are no findings from it to fix.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Not met under the criterion's definition: no tool varies sign.yml's inputs, and no test suite measures branch coverage of its validation step. The gate's checks are static (actionlint, shellcheck, zizmor and others), and CodeQL is static analysis.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: No memory-unsafe language is used: the repository is YAML workflows with embedded bash and Markdown.
english_justification: All documentation, code comments, issues and commit messages are in English. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are filed as issues, triaged, and either scheduled with a linked pull request or closed with the reason recorded; none are left unanswered.
external_dependencies_justification: The dependencies are the actions sign.yml and the stubs use, each pinned to a full commit SHA with its version in a comment (enforced by lint:action-pins), plus the organisation's shared workflows pinned the same way; Renovate reads exactly these pins. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
floss_license_justification: Released under 0BSD, a FLOSS licence: LICENSE at the root, full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt, per-file attribution in REUSE.toml, enforced in the gate by lint:licence and lint:reuse. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/LICENSE
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the decision model explicitly rather than aspirationally: one maintainer deciding in the open, significant decisions made in writing and in public before they are implemented (the docs-first standup, recorded as issues and pull requests), declined paths recorded with reasons so they are re-litigated against the record, and a written succession plan. It is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file, so it governs every repository that does not carry its own. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project site is this GitHub repository; there is no separate website or download site. Verified against the live URL on 2026-11-15: strict-transport-security with preload, a content-security-policy, x-frame-options: deny and x-content-type-options: nosniff. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
hardening_justification: sign.yml holds exactly id-token, attestations and artifact-metadata write and never contents: write; it checks out nothing and runs no caller code; every caller value is routed through env as UNTRUSTED_* and validated whitelist-style; predicate types are an explicit allowlist; every action is SHA-pinned. zizmor and lint:capability-boundary check this in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: The design is least privilege and minimal surface by construction: a separate repository whose one workflow runs no caller code, holds only the three scopes it needs, refuses anything not on its predicate allowlist and fails closed on malformed input, as README.md and the sign.yml header document. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
input_validation_justification: sign.yml validates every caller input against an allowlist before use: sha256sum records only (at most 1024), a lowercase image name with sha256:<64 hex>, predicate types only from its case statement, and a predicate only as one JSON object. Anything else fails the job. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/sign.yml
installation_common_justification: Installation uses the platform's standard convention for reusable workflows: a caller adds one `uses: monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml@<sha>` line and grants the three documented permissions; removal is deleting the line. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: `mise trust && mise install` brings the organisation's pinned toolchain and `mise run ci` runs exactly the check CI runs, per items 1 and 2 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: There is no installation system: the workflow is referenced in place by commit SHA and nothing is installed to a destination directory.
interact_justification: This repository has no health files of its own, so GitHub serves the organisation defaults here: CONTRIBUTING.md, SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, the issue forms and the pull-request template from monumental-archive/.github. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
interfaces_current_justification: Renovate keeps every action and shared-workflow pin current (the open Dependency Dashboard issue tracks them) and actionlint, run by lint:actions in the gate, fails on deprecated GitHub Actions features. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/renovate.json
internationalization_justification: The software is one reusable workflow with maintainer-facing log messages only; there are no end-user interface strings to localise.
know_common_errors_justification: The documented threat reasoning covers the error classes specific to this software: credential exfiltration through untrusted workflow input (enforced by zizmor and the capability-boundary lint), unpinned actions and supply-chain substitution (every uses: pinned to a full commit SHA with checksums and attestations), and secret exposure in logs. See docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/build-assessment.md.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designed and documented the project's security architecture: least privilege in workflows, an explicit capability boundary forbidding id-token: write in any workflow that runs caller-supplied code, keyless trusted publishing instead of long-lived tokens, and SLSA Build/Source/Dependency track conformance with written assurance in docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/release.md.
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and LICENSES/0BSD.txt in the REUSE-standard location; api.reuse.software reports this repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/LICENSE
license_per_file_justification: Every file carries an SPDX licence statement (0BSD) through REUSE.toml, with the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt; `reuse lint` reports 17 of 17 files with licence information and api.reuse.software reports the repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/REUSE.toml
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: Renovate keeps the pinned actions and shared workflows current (five canon updates merged on 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15), and the Monday audit re-runs the dependency advisory feed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/commits/main
maintenance_or_update_justification: Older versions stay usable forever: consumers pin a commit SHA, and a signature made at an older commit still verifies against it, as README.md explains. Upgrading is changing the SHA in one `uses:` line, which Renovate proposes in the consuming repository. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed. GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, trivy's secret rules run in the gate, and the design avoids long-lived credentials entirely: publishing is keyless via trusted publishing and OIDC.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Measured on 2026-11-15 over the whole history (all within six months): 6 `fix` commits. Two shipped with, or were closed by, a check that would catch a repeat: 0714ab7 (audit:signer-surface in the canon) and 1a28b69 (lint:runner-pin). The other four did not, so 2 of 6 (33%) is below the 50% required.
release_notes_justification: This repository publishes no releases and no tags: it is one reusable workflow, and every consumer pins it by full 40-hex commit SHA (`uses: monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml@<sha>`) and verifies with --signer-digest against that commit. The workflow is continuously updated and deployed to one place, which is the case this criterion allows N/A for; each change is described by its squash-merged pull request on main.
release_notes_vulns_justification: This repository publishes no releases and no tags: it is one reusable workflow, and every consumer pins it by full 40-hex commit SHA (`uses: monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml@<sha>`) and verifies with --signer-digest against that commit. There are no release notes to carry vulnerability identifiers, and no publicly known vulnerability in this workflow has been fixed.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands as a pull request with its own commits; the repository contains the full development history, not only released states.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, committer, timestamp and diff for every change; history is protected by org rulesets and every revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation (SLSA Source L3).
report_archive_justification: The issue tracker is public, permanently archived and searchable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bug reports go to this repository's GitHub Issues, using the issue forms the organisation serves as defaults; SUPPORT.md says where to ask. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/issues
report_responses_justification: Every issue filed in the last 12 months has been acknowledged and triaged by the maintainer; the tracker carries no unanswered reports.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, used for every individual issue. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/issues
require_2FA_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide — GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation — so it covers pushing to the repository and access to private vulnerability reports alike.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, served here as the organisation default, carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and what each is responsible for. The maintainer role is held by the @monumental-archive/owners team. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
secure_2FA_justification: The 2FA in use is cryptographic rather than SMS-based: GitHub's supported second factors here are TOTP and WebAuthn, and the organisation's requirement is satisfied without SMS.
security_review_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are security reviews written against this project's own security requirements and boundary, control by control, and docs/slsa-reference.md records what is claimed and what is deliberately not. They are current, not historical: the scheduled audit re-checks the claims they rest on. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
signed_releases_justification: This repository publishes no releases and no tags: it is one reusable workflow, and every consumer pins it by full 40-hex commit SHA (`uses: monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml@<sha>`) and verifies with --signer-digest against that commit. With no releases there is nothing to sign as a release. Each push to main receives a signed source-provenance link from source-attest.yml. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/source-attest.yml
sites_https_justification: The repository and its documentation are served by GitHub over HTTPS; there is no separate project website. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub; the project stores no passwords of its own.
small_tasks_justification: No small tasks are identified here: on 2026-11-15 this repository's only open issue is Renovate's Dependency Dashboard, and no issue carries 'good first issue'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/issues
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: zizmor is a vulnerability scanner specific to what this project produces — GitHub Actions workflows — covering template injection, excessive permissions, credential persistence and unpinned actions. CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide and trivy adds misconfiguration and secret rules. All run in the gate on every pull request.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Static code findings are fixed before merge, because the gate blocks the pull request; CodeQL has no open alert here. The four open code-scanning alerts are Scorecard posture checks (CodeReview, BranchProtection, Fuzzing, CII-Best-Practices), not vulnerabilities in the code. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL default setup runs on this repository, and the gate runs shellcheck over every run: block, actionlint and zizmor over every workflow and trivy over configuration on every pull request. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit: the gate runs on every pull request and every push to main, and a scheduled Monday audit re-runs the network-dependent checks.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is not measured: the only executable code is the bash in sign.yml's validation step, the repository has no .coverage-floor, and the gate's coverage:check reports 'no .coverage-floor, skipped'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: gate.yml runs the full organisation gate on every pull request, every push to main and in the merge queue, and it is a required check. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
test_invocation_justification: `mise run ci` is the one command, identical locally and in CI, documented in item 2 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most_justification: Statement coverage is not measured. The gate checks every tracked file statically (actionlint, shellcheck on every run: block, zizmor, capability and permission lints), but no test executes sign.yml's validation step, so coverage of it is unknown.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' item 3, is the formal written policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, and a lint, audit task or workflow assertion in configuration and policy repositories. It is stated as policy: the gate's checks are the specification, and functionality nothing enforces is functionality the next change may silently remove. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_policy_justification: Item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' is the policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - in a configuration repository such as this one, a lint, an audit task or an assertion in a workflow. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement coverage is not measured: the repository has no .coverage-floor and the gate's coverage:check skips it. The only executable code is the bash embedded in sign.yml's validation step, which no test executes. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Statement coverage is not measured (see test_statement_coverage80): no .coverage-floor, and no test executes sign.yml's validation step.
test_justification: Two automated, FLOSS suites. The gate (gate.yml, `mise run ci`) runs on every pull request and is static here: lint:actions (actionlint), lint:shell-embedded (shellcheck enable=all on every run: block), lint:zizmor, lint:capability-boundary, lint:caller-permissions, lint:action-pins, lint:yaml, lint:reuse, lint:trivy and the rest of the belt; coverage:check skips (no .coverage-floor). End to end, release-lab's exercise-sign.yml builds two fixtures, calls sign.yml at its pinned SHA across the repository boundary and verifies the result as a stranger would. That workflow runs on manual dispatch, not per change; its last run, 2026-08-13, succeeded. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/exercise-sign.yml
tests_are_added_justification: This repository's recent behaviour changes came with checks: removing verification_summary from the signing surface (0714ab7) came with the canon's audit:signer-surface, and pinning the signing job's runner (1a28b69) is held by lint:runner-pin. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/commit/0714ab7
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is stated in the documented instructions for change proposals themselves: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' - a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: With a single maintainer, no proposed modification is reviewed by a person other than its author. This is the Source L4 and Gold boundary for this project and is recorded as headcount-blocked in docs/slsa-reference.md; it is watched as an issue rather than papered over. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: The reused components are GitHub actions and the organisation's shared workflows, each pinned by full commit SHA with its version in a comment; Renovate opens the update pull request and the gate checks it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/renovate.json
version_semver_justification: No semantic version is used, by design: consumers pin and verify the signer by commit SHA (--signer-digest), because the commit is the identity that signatures bind to. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
version_tags_signed_justification: There are no version tags to sign: consumers pin this repository by commit SHA. Each commit on main instead receives a signed source-provenance link from source-attest.yml. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/source-attest.yml
version_tags_justification: No version tags are made: every consumer pins the full commit SHA and verifies the signature's --signer-digest against it, so a tag would add a mutable name to an identity that must stay fixed.
version_unique_justification: Each version consumers use is identified by its unique git commit SHA, which the criterion accepts as a version identifier: callers pin `sign.yml@<40-hex sha>` and verification checks the certificate's signer digest against that commit. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/README.md
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability is open (Dependabot reports 0 alerts on 2026-11-15); dependency-review blocks a newly introduced high-severity advisory on every pull request, and Renovate keeps the pins current. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There is no known unpatched vulnerability of medium or higher severity: Dependabot reports 0 alerts on 2026-11-15, Renovate updates the pins continuously, and trivy runs in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/renovate.json
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, so reports stay private until an advisory is published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the process: private reporting through the repository's Security tab. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months, so there is no response time to report. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 14 days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, what to expect afterwards, and the scope. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: The gate is a required check and red on any finding, so no warning merges. The one suppression is in level.yml, a zizmor dangerous-triggers ignore with its reasoning written beside it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
warnings_justification: The gate runs actionlint, shellcheck on every embedded run: block, zizmor, yamllint, typos, rumdl, editorconfig and REUSE over every tracked file, and any finding fails it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
warnings_strict_justification: Maximally strict for the languages present: lint:shell-embedded runs shellcheck with the organisation's enable=all and extended-analysis over every run: block in sign.yml and the stubs, actionlint restates the same flags, and zizmor runs at its default (all audits). Any finding fails the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/signer/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
